descriptions.text: Peapods Finance's pod token (ppPP) exposes a flash() function that transfers out the pod's underlying Peas tokens and invokes a callback() on the recipient before settling, without protecting against reentrant state changes. During the flash callback, the attacker re-entered the pod by calling bond() to mint pod (ppPP) shares against the very Peas tokens that had been flash-lent, while the flash loan's own bookkeeping had not yet been reconciled. By repeating the flash+bond loop, the attacker minted ppPP shares far in excess of the value actually deposited. The attacker then called debond() to redeem those inflated shares back into Peas, swapped Peas -> DAI -> WETH (with amountOutMinimum = 0). The root cause is the missing reentrancy guard / state validation in the flash-loan path, which allowed bonding using in-flight (borrowed) tokens.
